task: Add a shell-level UNLOCKED! reward screen between stages of the linear run, and show earned/unlocked/locked states in the Stamp Book
requirements: gameSequence.js: export UNLOCK_STAGE='unlock'; it is a non-game stage (backTarget null). In sequence mode, finish(gameId) records, then if nextGameAfter(gameId) is a game it shows UNLOCK_STAGE (transition:false, backAvailable:false) passing {completed, next} via show's options as `unlock`; the last game still goes straight to COMPLETE_STAGE with a transition. Hub mode is unchanged (finish -> hub, no unlock).
Navigator gains continueFromUnlock(): only acts when current===UNLOCK_STAGE; goes to the pending next game with the normal wipe transition. back(), restart(), enter() never show unlock.

Export pure stageProgressState(id, stamps, sequence=GAME_SEQUENCE) -> 'earned' | 'unlocked' | 'locked': earned if stamps[id]; else first stage is unlocked; else unlocked iff predecessor stamped; else locked.

New src/ui/stageUnlock.js createStageUnlock({root, lesson, strings, audio, onComplete, durationMs=1800}) controller (enter/update/exit like sequenceComplete.js): full-screen opaque celebratory card, big CSS/emoji open-lock icon, 'UNLOCKED!', large lesson.name. No buttons, no paragraph. Plays audio.playSfx('unlock') ~400ms after enter; calls onComplete once via setTimeout(durationMs) — never depends on animationend. exit clears timers.
styles.css: pop-in animations (lock shackle opens, text scales in); under prefers-reduced-motion: no animation, static open lock, same timing.

audio.js: add 'unlock' SFX distinguishable from complete/interact/accept: a short rising three-note triangle arpeggio (e.g. C6-E6-G6), gain ~0.1. Extend playSfx to support a `notes` list of steps if needed; existing SFX unchanged.
main.js: makeStage handles UNLOCK_STAGE using the unlock payload, onComplete: () => shellRoute.continueFromUnlock(). __eslDebug.shell keeps reporting stage ('unlock' while shown).

stampBook.js: per lesson render state from stageProgressState: earned keeps current presentation; unlocked shows ○ + 'UNLOCKED'; locked shows 🔒 + 'LOCKED', class is-locked, dimmed (not error-looking). Entries are not clickable. Strings go in UI.stampBook in lesson.js (English main labels).
Restaurant's どうぶつえんへ exit already calls ctx.finish, so it must route through the unlock with no Restaurant change.
Update scripts/playthrough-sequence.mjs so it tolerates/asserts the unlock stage between games and that Back never shows it.

Record the decision in DESIGN_DECISIONS.md (date 2026-10-18: shell unlock stage, no wipe into the card, derived stamp-book states, rejected: per-game unlock logic, persistent unlock DB, level select).
constraints: Do not modify any minigame under src/minigames/.
No new persistent storage; stamps are the source of truth.
No Continue button; no level-select from the Stamp Book.
Edit files only; do not commit.
Edit files with your structured patch/edit tool. If a shell-based edit fails once because of quoting or escaping, switch to the structured mechanism.
tests: each of coloring/restaurant/zoo/sports finish shows unlock with the correct next lesson, then continueFromUnlock enters it
drink-stand finish goes to complete with no unlock
back never shows unlock; restart starts at coloring; hub finish returns to hub
stageProgressState rules incl. coloring always unlocked, earned wins
stageUnlock auto-continues via timer with no animation events, shows lesson name, onComplete once
stamp book renders earned/unlocked/locked classes and labels

behavioralAcceptance.description: Controller views the unlock card in the browser and runs the sequence harness.

notes: Read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entries about the shell navigator / GAME_SEQUENCE (2026-09-28, 2026-10-17) before editing; minigames only call ctx.finish(result).

Current flow: navigator.finish -> record (recordFinish plays audio complete) -> go(next) with wipe via transitions.run. The unlock card replaces the finished game WITHOUT a wipe (opaque card covers the canvas), then the exit to the next game uses the normal wipe; total time stays ~2.4s.
The existing FakeElement DOM in gameSequence.test.mjs can be reused for UI tests; use fake timers (mock.timers from node:test) for the auto-continue test.
Kids are Japanese elementary students: big bold text, bright colours matching the existing sequence-complete card palette in styles.css.
